BACKGROUND

A little background

In Genie's release interview, Kang Asol says she wanted to ask whether others also knew the self-dislike she describes. Asking the question was itself an attempt to receive and offer comfort. The song appears on her 2018 album The Day of Love.

INSIDE THE LYRICS

An island without shelter

  • Isolation
  • Self-blame
  • Caring for oneself

The island offers no refuge: others cannot find or reach it, yet the speaker has nowhere to hide from the cold wind. Waves have swept them there. These details make being alone feel exposed and involuntary, rather than a peaceful retreat.

The lyric then turns from the landscape toward the parts of a person that remain difficult to care for. Looking inward only deepens the speaker’s loneliness, and everything seems to accuse them of being at fault. That sense of blame becomes another part of their loneliness.

The repeated question is whether they must go on living with a self that feels like an affliction. It receives no answer. In her Genie interview, Kang Asol describes wanting to ask whether others shared this feeling. The question reaches outward even while the island remains unreachable.

ABOUT THE ARTIST / 강아솔

Kang Asol

Kang Asol is a singer-songwriter whose songs explore loneliness, self-doubt and the wish to keep loving. She writes about feelings that reassurance does not always reach.

She recorded her first album in Jeju in 2012, then worked on her second in Seoul. Her third album, The Day of Love, followed in February 2018.
